articles.title: Man Utd 2-3 Brighton: Michael Carrick 'not bothered' by pressure after loss
articles.summary: Manager Michael Carrick insists he does not feel under pressure after Manchester United's EFL Cup exit.
articles.body:
Sir Alex Ferguson was St Mirren manager the last time Manchester United lost at Old Trafford having taken a 2-0 lead.

That is the context to the shocking Carabao Cup third-round exit his old club suffered against Brighton on Wednesday.

It is a period of time that encompasses the legendary Scot's dynasties at Aberdeen as well as United. The Class of '92 were in nappies when John Pratt scored the winner for Tottenham on 4 September 1976.

After holding protests inside and outside the ground before Sunday's loss to 10-man Manchester City, United supporters made their feelings known about their latest embarrassment in three ways.

Most fans simply left as the players embarked on their post-match lap of appreciation.

Some of those who remained booed, as they had done when their side fell behind 21 minutes from time.

By the time they approached the tunnel, close to United's 'singing section', supporters were asking Michael Carrick and his players 'what was that?'. Their wording was somewhat more colourful.

It is not certain where 15-year-old JJ Gabriel was while all this was taking place, but nothing happened that would make him think he had got it wrong by turning his back on the club.

Indeed, it is quite possible, probable indeed, that the promised senior debut would have been scrapped given the game situation - and the fact skipper Bruno Fernandes was among the experienced players introduced in the frantic final stages.

"Of course we can turn it around, we have got some really good players," said Carrick. "It feels bad because we haven't had a great week or two, or three weeks."

Man Utd lose to Brighton from 2-0 up to end 50-year record

'Let's go, let's go' - inside catastrophic derby VAR mistake

Carrick's side have won twice this season, against newly promoted Ipswich at home after falling behind, and Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK in the Champions League. They have now lost on three occasions, more defeats than he experienced in 17 matches after replacing Ruben Amorim in January.

He has been around Manchester United long enough to know the pressure losing runs can build.

"I don't feel under pressure," he said. "Either way, that doesn't bother me one bit.

"I understand what goes on outside and how the world works, but it doesn't bother me. What bothers me is winning games, having a good feeling around the place and a good feeling around the group to know we're moving in a good direction."

The problem is it doesn't feel as though they are moving in a good direction. There were certainly not many positives to take from this mess.

The obvious one was Shea Lacey, who marked his first senior start with a well-taken eighth-minute goal. It meant he became the first teenager to score on his first United start since Marcus Rashford in February 2016.

Lacey was one of eight changes made by Carrick. Defensively, those changes were not a success.

Diogo Dalot was one of the three players to keep their place. His form has deserted him. Noussair Mazraoui is the back-up left-back, which only heightens the debate over the wisdom not to buy one before the transfer window closed. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven looked like the inexperienced defenders they are. In midfield Manchester United were overrun.

Yet again, Rashford threatened without managing a goal or an assist. He came closest to levelling when he sped beyond the Brighton defence, but his shot was saved by Jason Steele.

"The longer the game went, the more we had control," was the concise assessment of Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler. "I thought we deserved to win."

His greatest sadness was for Lacey, who should have had his name in lights but instead was part of a team scuttling off the pitch to the sound of boos and harsher criticism.

"It's a shame that Shea's moment, such a great moment for him, for his family, his friends and the whole academy; to have an academy player come in and have a moment like that, gets a bit lost, unfortunately," said Carrick.

"It won't for him when things settle down but, as we sit here now, it feels that it was a long time ago."

Carrick also addressed the JJ Gabriel situation.

"He's a young boy, he's 15, and for me, definitely, and from a club point of view, looking after our younger players, their welfare, their wellbeing, their exposure, we've got to be really conscious of that in this situation," he explained.

But ultimately, for any manager, the assessment of their work comes through results.

"Being here toughens you up over a period of time," he said. "It depends how you deal with it. You've got to deal with it in a way where you can cope with it and you can bring out the best in yourself. However you do that, with your motivation and the confidence deep within yourself to know we can win football matches.

"We've gone out of the cup tonight, and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that. I'm honest enough to say that's how it feels. But it doesn't have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction."

Manchester United have one more game before the international break, at Fulham on Sunday.

For the general wellbeing of the club, Carrick's team really need to win.

Speaking on Sky Sports, former England midfielder Jamie Redknapp said he wasn't sure they will.

"Right now, they're miles off it," he said. "It doesn't matter how good the manager is, if you don't have the right players it makes it really difficult.

"There's a reason why the other managers have struggled. Sooner or later the pressure's always going to come on.

"This weekend becomes a huge game. He doesn't need another poor result, otherwise all of a sudden you're going into the international break and everyone's talking about you. The winners tonight are the players who didn't play."

articles.title: Man Utd 2-3 Brighton: Michael Carrick's Old Trafford tenure is only heading in one direction as Red Devils face familiar story
articles.summary: Man Utd crashed out of the Carabao Cup, surrendering a two-goal lead against Brighton to lose 3-2 at Old Trafford; it is the first time in 145 attempts where United have held a two-goal lead at Old Trafford and lost, ramping up the pressure on head coach Michael Carrick
articles.body:
"We've gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that," he said. "I'm happy enough to be honest about that. That's how it feels."

It's a story that's been seen before. A dismal Carabao Cup experience at the first hurdle - this time throwing away a 2-0 lead to exit to Brighton - harks back to memories of Ruben Amorim's disappointing defeat at Grimsby last year , which helped signal the beginning of the end.

A cup exit to the Seagulls was also reminiscent of the FA Cup defeat United suffered to Fabian Hurzeler's side at the start of the year. That was the last match before Carrick returned to the club and sparked a mini-revival. Now it seems like United are back to square one again.

Even Pascal Gross scoring the equaliser at Old Trafford brought back memories of how he netted twice at United's home in August 2022 to put Erik ten Hag's tenure on the back foot, in the same way Carrick is facing an uphill battle now.

Gross still doing the business four years later is a great testament to the German's longevity at 35 years old - but it's an even more damning reflection of United's lack of progression in that time.

Since that match in 2022, which came 1,502 days ago, Gross has secured European football for Brighton, left the club for Borussia Dortmund, rejoined the Seagulls, got them back into Europe, watched on as United spent £365m on seven new central midfielders - and still he stood tall above the United midfield.

Around £140m of that pot started for United against Brighton in Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount and Andrey Santos, while a further £70m in Carlos Baleba watched on from the stands as his old club beat his new one. What must he be thinking?

Just like against Hull on the opening weekend of the season, United were outfought by Brighton. "They didn't look fit enough," said Jamie Redknapp. "I don't know if a lot of them do enough. I saw too many players not running back or not looking fit enough."

Many can point towards the nine changes Carrick made, with many of United's players coming into the team after weeks on the Premier League bench. But Brighton also made six changes to their regular line-up, including first starts for the club to four summer signings. What was their excuse?

Once again, the lack of investment in the defensive positions during the transfer market was very clear. The warnings about not addressing that position were there - and a big reason for Brighton turning the game on its head was the defensive displays of Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven.

"The inexperience of the two young centre-backs definitely showed," said Redknapp. "The pair of them were just inept in everything they did. If you look at Luka Vuskovic, who is 18 or 19, at this level he has aggression, winning challenges, recovery runs.

"And you looked at the two who played at United who played like everything was easy, making bad decisions - there was a difference in Brighton's defending when it came to going about their business."

The difference was seen in the second goal, as Vuskovic won a header ahead of Benjamin Sesko and the ball ran straight through the heart of the United defence for Gross to score easily.

Heaven was caught on his heels and failed to come across. "He doesn't anticipate the danger. Sprint, get to the penalty spot. But he's jogging.

"And Yoro, what kind of an effort is that to stop the shot? How easy was that? This isn't a five-a-side competition."

And for the third goal, Yoro was caught jogging back again as Brighton broke to score - not only highlighting Redknapp's defensive concerns about United, but their fitness ones too. "You've got to sprint Leny," he said. "He's jogging. If he sprints, he gets back and makes that block."

But while United are making familiar mistakes, they are still making unwanted history.

Not only was this the first time in 50 years that an opposition team has won at Old Trafford having been 2-0 down in the game, but it was the first time United have lost at home after holding a half-time lead in 551 half-time leads.

The time before the defeat to Brighton came in 1984, which pre-dated Sir Alex Ferguson's time at the club. Throw in a joint-worst start to a Premier League season after four games and the pressure is really growing on Carrick.

United's only win so far this season has been a 5-2 win over Ipswich that saw United struggle for the best part of an hour. And while there have been some mitigating factors - worldies at Everton and a contentious Manchester derby winner - there have been too many of those to be one-offs already.

It all sets up a massive Super Sunday game this weekend away at winless Fulham, facing their own early woes under Alvaro Arbeloa. What follows is a three-week international break which is prime time for an early managerial change.

A win at Craven Cottage buys Carrick time. Defeat and it will be a long period of questions.

articles.title: Why Kalen DeBoer expects fast start for Alabama vs Florida State
articles.summary: Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer wants a faster start against Florida State after analyzing early season performances.
articles.body:
Alabama football plans to use the Kentucky team to set the tone for the remainder of its 2026 season.

In his weekly "Hey Coach" Crimson Tide Sports Network radio show, Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said the Wildcats helped Alabama realize "it isn't always going to be perfect." The introduction for SEC play — a 45-17 win against Kentucky — was textbook evidence of the resiliency and a team "built for the long haul."

But that is not what DeBoer is focused on heading into Week 3 against Florida State .

"We're going to dig a little deeper," DeBoer said. "I think our team truly believes and one of the things we talk about is as the game goes on, we will continue to get better. We want to be great going in."

Through two games, Alabama has scored 17 total points in the first quarter. But DeBoer is expecting a faster start, especially against a Florida State team the Crimson Tide opened the 2025 season against and lost.

"As our coaches get more and more information. and our players continue as we have more film each and every week of our opponent, I think they will be even more comfortable and you'll see even faster starts from our guys playing fast, knowing what to expect from their opponent," DeBoer said. "I'm looking forward to the next steps we take this week, really challenging our guys to come out, especially in Bryant-Denny Stadium and make some plays right away. Play confident. Play fast."

Alabama kicks off against Florida State at 2:30 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 19 on ABC.

articles.title: Broncos-Chiefs drew 23.2 million viewers on Monday night
articles.summary: The Monday Night Football opener drew a big audience, with the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos getting 23.2 million viewers.
articles.body:
The Monday Night Football opener drew a big audience, with the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Broncos getting 23.2 million viewers.

That number includes everyone who watched the main broadcast on ESPN and ABC, the ManningCast on ESPN2, the Spanish broadcast on ESPN Deportes and the stream on NFL+. ESPN did not announce how many viewers watched on each platform that showed the game.

It was ESPN's most-watched Monday Night Football Week 1 game and third-most watched Monday night game ever, although historical comparisons can be misleading because ratings today count out-of-home viewers who previously weren't counted.

This year's audience was 5 percent greater than last year's Week 1 Monday Night Football audience, which was 22.1 million viewers .

The pregame show Monday Night Countdown , had 1.9 million viewers, a 7 percent increase over Week 1 last year. That's a fairly small increase given that Monday Night Countdown now airs on both NFL Network and ESPN .

articles.title: Betis - Getafe | Bordalás mide el fondo de armario verdiblanco: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: Los de Pellegrini afrontan en La Cartuja el segundo de sus tres partidos de esta semana
articles.summary: Los de Pellegrini afrontan en La Cartuja el segundo de sus tres partidos de esta semana
articles.body: El Betis, que suma cuatro triunfos en las cinco primeras jornadas de Liga, recibe esta tarde en el Estadio de La Cartuja al Getafe con el objetivo de seguir con su gran momento de juego y resultados. Pero lo hará 'obligado' a rotar, con tres partidos en una misma semana, y también a cambiar de registro: enfrente no estarán equipos que dejan jugar como Real Madrid, Lille o Villarreal, a los que se enfrentó y consiguió ganar en la competición doméstica y en su estreno en la Champions League de la semana pasada en Francia, sino un adversario rocoso, que hace de la seguridad defensiva su punto fuerte y de los que obligan a trabajar el partido con calma... sin caer en la precipitación Después de su victoria ante los de Mourinho y de estrenar su regreso a la Champions League con una brillante remontada en Francia, los de Pellegrini firmaron en La Cerámica el lunes su partido más completo en lo que va de curso, con hasta 26 remates. La máquina verdiblanca parece perfectamente engrasada y todo apunta a que esta tarde llegarán las rotaciones. Aunque por ahora no podrá contar con Diego Llorente ni con Ruibal, lesionados, el Ingeniero tiene a casi toda su plantilla disponible en busca de un triunfo que le permita seguir muy arriba en la clasificación. Ortiz, Junior, Valentín, Facundo, Antony y Parrott, apunta a estar entre las posibles novedades del once. El Getafe visita un feudo como La Cartuja, llamado a ser uno de los más complejos y complicados de toda la categoría. El conjunto azulón quiere dar la sorpresa y, tras dos empates consecutivos en casa, llega a Sevilla con hambre de tres puntos. Bordalás recupera a Zaid Romero, que no estuvo contra el conjunto herculino, aunque seguirá contando, al menos, con las bajas de los jugadores lesionados que no estuvieron el pasado domingo. Además, el alicantino desveló en sala de prensa que tenía otros hombres aún tocados y que esperaría hasta hoy para ver si finalmente viajaban o no a la capital andaluza. Álvaro Valles vs. David Soria: Son dos de los mejores guardametas de LaLiga. El de La Rinconada pasó un año en blanco en Las Palmas para cumplir su sueño de volver al Betis y se ha terminado convirtiendo en una pieza clave para Pellegrini, con intervenciones de mucho mérito. El madrileño, con pasado en el Sevilla, es el dueño indiscutible de la meta azulona desde hace casi una década y es clave en sus éxitos. Seis goles encajados y tres porterías a cero en cinco jornadas para el guardameta de los andaluces, y otros seis tantos en contra, pero sólo un partido sin encajar para el de los madrileños. * Estadísticas de Documentación MARCA, Opta, Bdfutbol y Whoscored

articles.summary: Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras are through to yet another Copa Libertadores semifinal, the 13th in their history.Extending their record among Brazilian clubs....
articles.body:
Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras are through to yet another Copa Libertadores semifinal, the 13th in their history.

Extending their record among Brazilian clubs.

After winning at Nubank Parque (1-0), Verdão traveled to Quito and its altitude to take on LDU.

They saw the Ecuadorian side make it 3-2 after the 90 minutes, which forced a penalty shootout.

But they came out on top in the shootout (4-3) thanks to Carlos Miguel .

Verdão will now face Fluminense, chasing their fourth Libertadores final since the 2020 edition.

LDU did what was expected of them: they pressed from the start.

Andreas was the first to try to catch them out - forcing Valle into a reaction save.

And it was up to Marlon Freitas to capitalize on an opposition mistake and score (10').

The problem (for Verdão) was seeing that lead disappear shortly after.

Set piece, too much room for Segovia, and 1-1 in the 15th minute.

LDU began to take control against a Palmeiras side that could not keep possession well enough to "breathe".

Verdão kept trying. But without creating any real danger.

And they went into the break still celebrating the fact they remained ahead.

LDU fail to threaten and... Tigrinho gets them!

The home side continued to enjoy more possession after the break.

But without creating any real danger thanks to improved Palmeiras defending.

Brought on in the 67th minute, Vitor Roque did not take long to deliver, offering more movement and aggression.

And he put Verdão back in front after the penalty conceded by Minda.

He leveled it in the 45th minute of the second half after pouncing on a Carlos Miguel rebound.

And he made it 3-2 in the 48th, once again in the air.

Verdão moved ahead right after LDU's second penalty thanks to their goalkeeper.

But then Lucas Evangelista saw Valle steal the spotlight.

And Carlos Miguel came up big once more on the Ecuadorian side's final kick, denying Segovia (4-3).

Verdão will be at home in the second and decisive clash against Fluminense for a place in the Libertadores final.

The matches will be played between October 13 and 22.

As for the grand final - against Corinthians, Estudiantes, Flamengo or Independiente del Valle - it will be on November 28.

And the stage will be the Centenario, in Montevideo.

articles.title: Dodgers owner Mark Walter sells off shares of Chelsea weeks after surprise Lakers sale amid investigation
articles.summary: Mark Walter and his companies are currently under federal investigation.
articles.body:
Mark Walter has officially sold off his shares in Chelsea .

Walter and co-owner Todd Boehly sold their shares in the English soccer club on Wednesday to majority owner Clearlake Capital, the team announced . Walter and Boehly purchased the club in 2022 alongside Clearlake Capital for roughly $3.3 billion.

Boehly was previously the chairman of Chelsea. Clearlake will now take controlling ownership of the club. It's unclear how much Walter sold his shares for, but the deal comes amid what's been a turbulent time for him.

Walter sold the Los Angeles Lakers for a record $12.5 billion to a group led by Josh Kushner and Bob Iger last month in a surprise move. The deal reportedly came together in a matter of days, and ended Walter's time running the franchise after roughly a year. He had purchased the franchise for a then-record $10 billion in June 2025.

Walter is the subject of a federal investigation into whether his insurance companies engaged in fraud. There are allegations that they invested money from policyholders into other companies owned by Walter without properly disclosing it to investors. Walter has also been accused of accusations that he used those companies, and that money, to fund his purchase of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Walter's company, TWG Global, said last month after the sale of the Lakers that the Dodgers are not going to be sold, and that it complied with all MLB rules when they purchased the Dodgers for more than $2 billion in 2012. Dodgers president Stan Kasten has reiterated that the Dodgers are "not for sale" despite the investigation into Walter, too.

But after selling off two of the three most notable teams that he owns, even with the team insisting otherwise, it's fair to wonder if the Dodgers could be sold in the near future, too. The Dodgers have already clinched a playoff spot this fall, and are vying for a third straight World Series title.

Chelsea is coming off a successful year, too. The club recently won the FIFA Club World Cup and the UEFA Europa Conference League. They currently sit at 2-1-1 in the Premier League after a 2-2 draw with Hull City on Sunday.

articles.title: José Alberto: "Creía que el equipo iba a poder competir a mejor nivel"
articles.standfirst: "Hemos dado demasiadas facilidades en defensa", dice el técnico
articles.summary: "Hemos dado demasiadas facilidades en defensa", dice el técnico
articles.body: El entrenador del Racing de Santander, José Alberto, ha apuntado a las "demasiadas facilidades defensivas" de su equipo como la clave de la derrota de este miércoles frente al Barcelona (7-2). "No ha sido nuestro mejor día. Nos ha faltado competir a un poco más de nivel. Sobre todo en defensa hemos dado demasiadas facilidades, la muestra son los tres penaltis cometidos y los dos goles de tiros exteriores", ha resumido el preparador asturiano. José Alberto ha destacado que "a nivel ofensivo en pocos momentos" fueron ellos mismos, aunque generaron "las ocasiones suficientes para marcar algún gol más", si bien ha remarcado que deben "hacer las cosas mejor y ser un equipo más riguroso" para puntuar en un escenario así. "La sensación que tengo es que cada ve que amenazábamos con recortar el marcador, pisaban el acelerador y se separaban otra vez. Están en un momento de confianza extraordinario que es muy difícil de parar", ha añadido. José Alberto ha señalado que tiene "la responsabilidad absoluta" por el rendimiento de su equipo tras introducir ocho cambios en la alineación. "Creía que el equipo iba a poder competir a mejor nivel, pero no hemos sido capaces. Con tres partidos esta semana, quería acercar a la gente que tiene menos minutos, porque sino es muy difícil poder hacerlo", ha comentado el entrenador, que ha señalado la necesidad de "ser más duros" pese a que "todo el mundo ha dado la cara". Sobre el hecho de no haber introducido sustituciones al descanso, ha argumentado que "era injusto señalar jugadores" y prefirió "dar continuidad al equipo" que, en su opinión, entró "bastante bien" a la segunda mitad. "Estamos haciendo la pretemporada con la temporada empezada porque tenemos once jugadores nuevos, pero LaLiga no perdona y tenemos que competir. Lo que tengo claro es que el equipo no va a tener ninguna duda el próximo partido", ha reconocido. Por último, el técnico ha valorado que el Barça "reventó" a su equipo tras pérdida y en las situaciones de balón parado, y ha añadido que el equipo azulgrana, pese a la competencia que espera del Real Madrid y del Atlético por el título de Liga, está "mostrando todos los partidos que está a un nivel impresionante".

articles.summary: "Had the protocols been followed, the outcome of the game would have been different," FBS Oversight Committee said about Michigan vs Western Michigan.
articles.body:
Michigan football will remain the winner over Western Michigan – the Wolverines won 13-12 on a 47-yard Hail Mary from Bryce Underwood to JJ Buchanan as time expired – however it's not what should have happened.

So says the FBS Oversight Committee, which issued a statement Wednesday, Sept. 16, on the controversial ending to the Wolverines' Week 1 opener Sept. 5. While the overarching point is outcomes cannot be overturned after officials have declared a game has ended, embedded in the committee's response was an acknowledgment that the final play should not have happened.

"The committee consulted with national officiating leadership regarding the instant replay protocols," the statement reads in part. "Based on that information, the committee agreed that the instant replay protocols were not followed in the contest's second-to-last play. Had the protocols been followed, the outcome of the game would have been different."

In essence, if the officiating had gone as the governing body says it should, Western would've won 12-7 as a four-touchdown road underdog. But perhaps what's most relevant is there's nothing the NCAA can do about it. As much is stated in two separate bylaws, which say a final is a final and there's nothing in their power that allows them to change a result.

Rule 1-1-3-b: When the referee declares that the game is ended, the score is final.

Rule 5-2-9: No rule decision may be changed after the ball is next legally snapped, legally free-kicked or the second or fourth periods have ended.

Western Michigan officials said in a press conference the following day they weren't going to appeal, given there was no process to do so. However, a few days later, the Mid-American conference changed course and issued a statement saying the league was going to seek justice via an appeal and request the NCAA and FBS Oversight Committee "recognize Western Michigan as the actual winner of the game for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations, and take such other corrective action as may be within their authority."

In the end, nothing will change. Michigan used its sloppy play as motivation heading into Week 2 and rebounded with an impressive 17-10 upset win over previously 10th ranked Oklahoma. U-M, which had fallen out of the US LBM Coaches Poll following its debacle against WMU, vaulted all the way back up to No. 19 in the rankings heading into its Week 3 matchup against UTEP (3:30 p.m., Big Ten Network).

Western Michigan, meanwhile, took out its frustrations on Monmouth, pummeling the Hawks 49-14. The Broncos (1-1) now prepare to play Rice on the road in Houston this upcoming weekend.

articles.title: La calamidad de Szczesny: se enreda con Zabiri en unos de los fallos de la temporada y regala un gol
articles.summary: Wojciech Szczesny, que saltó al césped para suplir al lesionado Joan García, se lio en un despeja y se puso a intentar regatear en el Zabiri. El delantero del Racing Zabiri roba y marca para poner el 4-2, en un partido que el Barcelona acabó ganando 7-2.
articles.body: Wojciech Szczesny, que saltó al césped para suplir al lesionado Joan García, se lio en un despeja y se puso a intentar regatear en el Zabiri. El delantero del Racing Zabiri roba y marca para poner el 4-2, en un partido que el Barcelona acabó ganando 7-2. Hansi Flick, entrenador del F.C. Barcelona, fue preguntado por el sonado error de Szczesny en el segundo tanto del Racing. El técnico alemán le quitó importancia: "La próxima vez lo hará mejor. Esto es fútbol". Flick explicó que Joan García será sometido a más pruebas para conocer el alcance de dichas molestias, si bien espera que esté disponible con vistas al próximo encuentro liguero frente al Sevilla.

articles.title: Palacios: "Los directores deportivos somos como los bomberos, siempre estamos apagando fuegos"
articles.standfirst: El armero asegura que no puede desconectar de su trabajo
articles.summary: El armero asegura que no puede desconectar de su trabajo
articles.body: Desde que César Palacios aterrizó en Ipurua en el verano de 2021, sólo Barcelona, Real Madrid y Atlético han sumado más puntos que el Eibar en el fútbol profesional. Se quedó a un punto del ascenso directo en sus tres primeros cursos y pese a los importantes ajustes económicos que ha tenido el club para reducir las pérdidas, ha sabido reinventarse para mantener el sello competitivo que acompaña al club armero desde su llegada. Pregunta. Como futbolista y director deportivo siempre ha sido una persona de proyectos largos y de sentimiento de pertenencia. ¿Qué ha encontrado en el Eibar para echar raíces? Respuesta. Siento desde el principio ese grado de sentimiento y de implicación por el proyecto y por los valores del club. Todos los equipos en los que he estado tienen una manera de ser con la que me siento identificado. Lo único que intento es dar todo lo que tengo con mi trabajo para que el club pueda ir mejor. Pregunta. Ya son seis temporadas. La ilusión pesa más que el desgaste, ¿no? Respuesta. El desgaste emocional es muy grande porque vives las 24 horas de los 365 días del año pensando en fútbol. Sacrificas muchas cosas y estás señalado por todo. La del director deportivo es una profesión que comparo con la del bombero. Siempre estás apagando los fuegos que aparecen. Tengo la suerte de tener grandes compañeros alrededor mío. El fútbol lo identifico desde el sentimiento de equipo y en el Eibar eso está por encima de la individualidad. Pregunta. ¿Es capaz de desconectar su trabajo? Respuesta. Quedaría muy bien decirte que sí, pero no lo consigo. El fútbol ha sido mi vida desde siempre. Además, tengo la suerte de que mi hijo también está en el mundo del fútbol, por lo que es difícil que no vivamos todo al máximo. En verano no tienes vacaciones como tal, porque estás pendiente de las operaciones que están en marcha y de las planificaciones y durante la temporada siempre estás centrado en lo que pasa el fin de semana. Pregunta. Ha cambiado mucho el fútbol desde que usted comenzó como director deportivo. ¿Qué diferencias ve con respecto a sus inicios en el Numancia? Respuesta. En Soria pasé en tres días de ser jugador a ser director deportivo. Entonces, no teníamos plataformas ni imágenes de jugadores para poder firmar. Tenías que pedir CD a las personas que habían hecho la grabación de un partido. El fútbol ha evolucionado muchísimo. Ahora tenemos plataformas de visionado y control de datos. La inmediatez, la presión y la paciencia no son las mismas que antes. El fútbol es un reflejo de la sociedad y eso hace también que las decisiones que tomes requieran a veces tener tranquilidad, responsabilidad y análisis suficiente para no dejarte llevar por los momentos. Pregunta ¿Nota una presión añadida cuando se abre el mercado y tiene que mover las fichas del tablero? Respuesta. La presión la sientes durante todo el año porque es algo en lo que llevas trabajando toda la temporada. El fútbol tiene una cosa increíble y es que la misma noche que acaba la temporada ya estás tomando decisiones para la siguiente. No tienes ni un momento para celebrar o pasar el duelo. Cada mercado es distinto. Este año afrontábamos un verano tranquilo, con el bloque hecho, pero de repente surgió la marcha de San José. Las circunstancias inesperadas que aparecen es la adrenalina que nos mueve. La presión es la que se marca cada uno y la mía es hacerlo mejor posible por todas las personas que están trabajando en el club y por la afición. Pregunta. ¿De las seis incorporaciones que han hecho cuántas estaban en su cabeza en mayo? Respuesta. Cinco. Pregunta. Ser mejores reduciendo gastos es una misión complicada, ¿no? Respuesta. Nosotros no tenemos capacidad para asumir traspasos y tenemos que buscar jugadores libres. El coste de plantilla este año tenía que ser menor por las circunstancias económicas. Es difícil que un jugador que haya destacado mucho en Segunda División nosotros podamos incorporarlo. Si Elgezabal no hubiese tenido un año tan difícil hubiese sido difícil que hoy estuviese con nosotros. Pero somos un club respetado, el nombre del Eibar tiene fuerza y haber sumado una Ciudad Deportiva como la de Areitio también nos hace sumar más posibilidades. Pregunta. La mayoría de los directores deportivos apuran hasta el último día para firmar jugadores y luego está usted, que aparece con fichajes como el de Llorente o Bernat cuando los demás están de 'vacaciones'. Respuesta. Es que el mercado no se acaba el 1 de septiembre. Hace poco vi lista de jugadores que estaban libres y hay nombres interesantes e importantes. Por eso digo que no descansas nunca. Hay directores deportivos que prefieren esperar hasta el final con el riesgo de que la operación no pueda salir. Nosotros intentamos tomar las decisiones antes porque le damos mucha importancia al grupo humano y cuanto antes lo tengamos, mucho mejor. Siempre recuerdo una frase que me dijeron cuando me convertí en director deportivo y es que, si te funcionan más del 50% de los fichajes, ya tienes muy buen porcentaje. A veces nos olvidamos de que sólo juegan once y todos no pueden salir, aunque cuando ficho un jugador lo hago con la ilusión de que vaya a ser importante. Pregunta. Todo el mundo se queja de que no se cierre el mercado cuando empieza la competición, pero cada verano estamos en la misma situación. Respuesta. A mí me gustaría que cuando empiece la competición se cierre el mercado porque vivimos dos o tres semanas de incertidumbre. Los puntos del 16 de agosto valen lo mismo que los de abril. Entiendo que la industria del fútbol es enorme y no es fácil cuadrar todos los mercados. Otra cosa que tengo clara es que en los mercados de enero no se debería cambiar tanto las plantillas. Tendría que haber un tope de movimientos en invierno para cubrir lesiones y hacer algún retoque. Las planificaciones son para toda la temporada y no puede ser que, a mitad de enero, porque tengas una mayor capacidad económica cambies la mitad de la plantilla. Pregunta. ¿Cómo gestionaron la marcha de San José? Respuesta. En la renovación de Beñat dejamos una cláusula de salida a Primera. Pensaba que si ocurría algo sería al inicio del verano. De los banquillos de Primera, el único que estaba libre era el del Rayo y los rumores situaban a Jagoba Arrasate, al que tengo un aprecio enorme y es amigo mío. De un día para otro nos llegó que estaban valorando esa situación y se acabó dando. Fue un golpe a la planificación de decisiones que se habían tomado, pero en el fútbol no puedes hacer otra cosa que tomar decisiones y buscar soluciones. El club recibió un dinero por su marcha y no es habitual que los entrenadores dejen dinero por sus ventas. Pregunta. ¿Qué les sedujo de Aranbarri? Respuesta. Antes de que renovara Beñat ya trabajamos situaciones que podrían darse en el caso de que decidiera no continuar. Cuando se confirmó su marcha al Rayo, tuvimos que volver a ese momento. Ya se habían tomado decisiones en otros equipos y opciones que te habías planteado en otros momentos ya no estaban disponibles. Jokin no era la única opción que estuvo en la mesa, pero hicimos una apuesta por él desde el convencimiento, el conocimiento que teníamos en él y porque sabíamos de todas sus capacidades. Estaba la incertidumbre de que no había estado en el mundo profesional, pero apostar con alguien con experiencia tampoco es garantía de nada. El tiempo dirá si habremos acertado o no, pero estamos contentos de apostar por gente de casa. Pregunta. Es contradictorio que los entrenadores sean los jefes del vestuario y su cláusula sea más baja que la de cualquier jugador. Respuesta. También son puestos mucho más inestables. Los entrenadores tienen un riesgo mucho más grande que los jugadores. Las cláusulas que ponemos son acordes a la inestabilidad del cargo. Tampoco los entrenadores son los que tienen mejores contratos normalmente. Cada caso es un mundo, pero normalmente los clubes no acceden a pagar por un entrenador. Casi siempre se fijan en los que están libres. En este caso, el Rayo hizo la apuesta. El tema de las cláusulas son negociaciones. En algunas puedes estar más fuerte, en otras tienes que pensar que es mejor llegar a acuerdos. Somos un club que necesitamos equilibrar nuestros presupuestos. Tenemos que estar abiertos a situaciones de que haya traspasos y, en este caso, del entrenador. Y tomarlo dentro de la normalidad. Pregunta: 12 puntos de 15 posibles y lo mejor es que el equipo se parece mucho al de la última segunda vuelta. Respuesta. Gran parte de este grupo consiguió que en diciembre estuviéramos en descenso y acabáramos soñando con jugar los ‘playoffs’. No somos tan malos como podía parecer tras perder contra el Tenerife ni tan buenos por ganar cuatro partidos. Estamos con bajas de jugadores importantes y seguimos funcionado bien. Esa es nuestra fuerza. No tenemos que mirar más allá de la siguiente jornada. Vamos a seguir con nuestra idea, que nos sintamos identificados todos con lo que se ve en el campo sin perder el respeto a la Segunda. No vamos a meternos más presión de la que tenemos nosotros. Pregunta. ¿A qué atribuye el salto defensivo que dio el equipo la pasada temporada? Respuesta. Beñat se dio cuenta de que con su idea no nos estaba llegando y tomó decisiones. Situó a Arbilla de lateral izquierdo, metió a Peru de central, un doble pivote desde Sergio y Lander. El empate a cero en Córdoba fue muy importante. No fue un partido bonito, pero nos hizo ver que podíamos ser estables. Desde ahí crecimos y aprendimos a disfrutar también cuando nos tocaba defender. A mí me alegra muchísimo ver cómo defiende el equipo y cómo celebra cada acción defensiva. En los primeros años éramos el equipo a batir y teníamos la obligación de ir siempre al ataque. Los propios jugadores tampoco tenían esa mentalidad. Ahora hemos demostrado que sabemos defender en bloque bajo. Nos gusta ir alto, pero no se puede hacerlo durante los 90 minutos. El año pasado dimos un paso al frente en ese aspecto del juego y esa fue una de nuestras bazas. Por eso hay que mantener las cosas buenas que tenemos. Cuantas más herramientas tengamos para poder afrontar los partidos, mucho mejor. Hay que ser versátiles porque el fútbol te lleva a eso. Pregunta. ¿Las nuevas normas arbitrales favorecen el dinamismo del juego? Respuesta. Me gustan porque no se puede favorecer al mentiroso. Ahora no hay tantos problemas de isquios al final de los partidos. Todos los cambios que sean para mejorar, bienvenidos sean, pero sin perder la esencia de lo que es el fútbol. No me gusta un fútbol tan controlado con decisiones arbitrales. El fútbol es contacto, agresividad e ir a los duelos.

articles.title: Champions League performance won’t make or break Vincent Kompany’s future at Bayern Munich
articles.summary: The FC Bayern coach probably just needs to avoid a disaster.
articles.body:
Brad Friedel believes Vincent Kompany should have some breathing room at Bayern Munich, even if the Champions League does not ultimately end with the trophy coming back to Bavaria.

There is always pressure at Bayern Munich. The club is expected to dominate the Bundesliga, and the Champions League is naturally where the expectations become even greater. For supporters and the board, European success is the ultimate measuring stick.

But according to Friedel, simply failing to win the Champions League should not automatically put Kompany's job in danger.

The former United States goalkeeper believes the circumstances surrounding a potential elimination matter just as much as the result itself. A disappointing early exit would understandably raise questions, but losing a dramatic tie against one of Europe's best teams is an entirely different situation.

"There's pressure anytime you're at Bayern or PSG . Every now and again Leipzig or Dortmund push Bayern in the Bundesliga, but by and large Bayern are expected to dominate. Real Madrid and Barcelona face the same expectations, with only clubs like Atletico Madrid or Valencia occasionally challenging them. Because of that, the Champions League is massive for the board and supporters," Friedel told Jackpot City Casino . "If Bayern don't win it, there will naturally be pressure on Vincent Kompany, and he knows that. But it's always about the manner in which you lose. Their two legs against PSG, especially the first leg, was one of the most magnificent games of football I've ever watched. If that happens in a semi-final, would you fire a manager for that? No, in my opinion. It was two heavyweights going blow for blow.

"The front three for both Bayern and PSG rated over 8.2 on match data, which rarely happens in top-level matches. If they were to go out 4-0 on aggregate in the round of 16, I could understand the board making a change, but not if they reach the semi-finals and lose a thriller against another top side."

Friedel pointed specifically to Bayern Munich's memorable Champions League meetings with Paris Saint-Germain as an example of the type of defeat that should not lead to a managerial change. Those matches were played at an incredibly high level, with both teams producing outstanding attacking performances.

That distinction could become particularly important if Bayern Munich makes another deep run under Kompany.

If Bayern Munich reaches the semifinals and goes out in a thrilling, closely contested battle against another European heavyweight, Friedel does not believe the board should view that as a reason to move on from Kompany. There is a significant difference between being outclassed and simply losing a great football match.

At the same time, Friedel acknowledges that patience has its limits. An ugly 4-0 aggregate elimination in the round of 16 would create a completely different conversation.

For Kompany, then, the Champions League objective is not necessarily as simple as win it or get fired. The manner of the performance could ultimately determine how much pressure he faces.

And considering the level of competition Bayern Munich will encounter in Europe, that could be an important distinction for the Belgian coach.

articles.title: Do Celtic have 'big issues', or will next four days hush concerns?
articles.summary: Chris Sutton believes his former side have "great concerns" despite a winning start to the Scottish Premiership season. The next four days will tell us whether those worries are justified.
articles.body:
Football in Glasgow's goldfish bowl has a habit of being unnecessarily dramatised, yet there is a case for saying a week in mid-September could have a defining impact on Celtic's season.

After spectacularly failing the first of three tests during this mini crucial spell, alarm bells are ringing among sections of an unconvinced support.

Martin O'Neill's side have the chance to right the wrongs of their sobering 3-0 Premier Sports Cup quarter-final defeat by Rangers at Ibrox when they host their city rivals in a rematch in the league on Sunday, but a Europa League opener with Ferencvaros comes first.

Celtic fans are tiptoeing with trepidation into their first European action since their Champions League play-off collapse in Linz, a capitulation that has the same supporters questioning this team's big-game credentials, especially after Sunday.

"It's strange you're never asked about team selection when you win games," O'Neill responded bullishly when asked about the outside noise.

"We've been doing a fair amount of winning domestically now for quite some considerable time and we've won our league games so far.

"It's another big test for us on Sunday, obviously, but it's amazing the number of times you're not questioned when you've won."

McGregor laments Celtic's 'team of individuals'

Celtic & Scotland legend McGrain diagnosed with Alzheimer's

Visit our Celtic page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

In short: the aforementioned big-game results this season and the performance level under O'Neill since January.

The 74-year-old's remit last term was to end a chaotic, rollercoaster campaign on a high after the Wilfried Nancy debacle. He absolutely did that, winning the Scottish Premiership title and Scottish Cup.

Celtic fans spent the aftermath of that double triumph torn over whether they wanted to watch their legendary manager head off into the sunset with two medals round his neck or have him lead the team into a fresh season. Even O'Neill was unsure .

One thing supporters were united on, though, was wanting to see overdue progress in Europe and a better product on the pitch. It seems they are still waiting for that.

Listen to live match commentary on BBC Sounds and follow text updates on the BBC Sport website and app.

There will be fans of rival clubs who will view those wishes as greed, given Celtic still continue to dominate domestically.

However, supporters of the Parkhead side have spent the past decade being conditioned into watching their team clean up trophies while still delivering dominant, free-flowing football, hence the demand is there.

O'Neill and his staff were largely given a pass last term during a season of intense turbulence. Fury was mostly directed towards the club's hierarchy, but the manager and his backroom team are now not immune from scrutiny.

The Celtic boss's team selection has been questioned by fans and pundits, including one of his former players, Chris Sutton, in the wake of an abject derby display.

Are Sutton's 'great concerns' justified?

Below-par showings were forgiven last season as Celtic simply just had to get by to stay in touch at the top before eventually leapfrogging Heart of Midlothian on the final day with a seventh successive league victory.

That Premiership-winning streak has been extended to 13 games following six straight victories to start the campaign, but concerns about performance level remain. Four of those six wins have been by a one-goal margin.

Twelve goals over three wins at Kilmarnock, Dundee United and in the first leg of the Champions League play-off against LASK sent an ominous warning to Celtic's domestic rivals amid a period of high spending, particularly in forward areas.

Camilo Duran has been the standout summer recruit so far with six goals and three assists in 10 appearances, while record signing Kasper Hogh and fellow big-money arrival Haissem Hassan are yet to fully settle.

Sutton said his old club have been "flat-track bullies" by "beating the teams you expect them to beat", but the collapse in Austria, plus Sunday's bruising loss, has highlighted glaring deficiencies.

Even captain Callum McGregor lamented Celtic's "team of individuals" after the weekend defeat at Ibrox.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club , former striker Sutton also expressed his "great concerns" for O'Neill's men and said they have "big issues" after a "lightweight" midfield was "run all over" by Rangers.

Celtic have struggled to build up play against coherent pressing teams, which results in opposition sides being offered too much encouragement when the ball turns over.

They faced a whopping 60 shots across both legs with LASK. Forty of them came in a mess of a second leg. In the Premiership alone this season, they have faced 64 attempts, the same number as Hearts and six more than Rangers.

Over just six games, that tally already makes up almost a quarter of the total they faced in the entirety of the 2024-25 league-winning campaign under Brendan Rodgers.

That said, in comparison to last term, which was overseen by Rodgers, Nancy and O'Neill, Celtic's Premiership numbers show they are currently averaging a far better goal concession rate while scoring and shooting more.

Come Sunday, though, the most crucial statistic could be in the points column.

With a rapid rematch against Rangers offering the chance to move eight points clear of their city rivals after a test against European-level opposition, the next four days will at least be mood-shifting.

Whether that is to O'Neill's benefit remains unclear.
